outlooks.summary: Large hail, damaging gusts, and a few tornadoes are all possible over the upper Mississippi Valley region today into this evening.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Recent surface analysis placed a low over eastern SD, with a dryline extending south-southwestward across eastern NE, central KS, far western OK, and into the TX Permian Basin. A cold front also extends southwestward from this low across central NE, far northwest KS, and into southeast CO. This surface low is forecast to move northeastward throughout the day, reaching northwestern MN by the early afternoon and western Ontario by this evening. The attendant cold front is expected to sweep eastward, and by 00Z this front will likely extend southward from western Ontario across central MN and then back southwestward across IA into central KS. This front will act as the impetus for thunderstorms as it interacts with the moist and buoyant air mass across the Upper MS Valley.

sections.title: Upper MS Valley
sections.text: Ongoing thunderstorm cluster moving across northern WI is expected to continue progressing northeastward for the next few hours. Downstream buoyancy will likely remain high enough for storm persistence, with at least some chance of isolated hail and/or damaging wind gusts reaching as far east as western portions of Upper MI. As the surface low mentioned in the synopsis moves northeastward, a moist low-level air mass will advect northward. As a result, low 70s dewpoints will likely be in place ahead of the approaching front across southern MN, with upper 60s dewpoints reaching into central MN. This low-level moisture combined with temperatures in the mid to upper 80s will result in strong instability across the region. Convective initiation appears likely as the front interacts with this buoyancy, although the warm temperatures aloft (possibly around -8 or -9 deg C at 500 mb this afternoon) and background rising heights could limit the overall coverage. Vertical shear will also be quite strong over the region, and the overall environment supports supercells capable of all severe hazards, including very large hail and tornadoes, with any storms that do develop. Highest probabilities

sections.text: Nudged 10-percent tornado probabilities to north of the IA/MN border and included a few counties north of MSP in the 10-percent tornado area (ENH categorical). ..Smith.. 05/09/2022 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1134 AM CDT Mon May 09 2022/

outlooks.summary: Large hail, damaging gusts, and a few tornadoes remain possible over the upper Mississippi Valley region this evening.

sections.title: 01z Update
sections.text: Mid-level short-wave trough is ejecting northeast across the northern Plains as 500mb speed max translates across the Dakotas into northwestern MN/western ON late this evening. Heights will begin to rise in the wake of this feature which should result in a slow-moving surface front/dryline trailing across IA into southeast NE. Over the last hour or so, convection has gradually deepened along the boundary near the MN/IA border and towers are building ahead of the wind shift into central IA. It appears organized convection, along with the threat for severe, will spread/develop south where steep lapse rates and ample buoyancy currently reside. Otherwise, severe threat is waning quickly with frontal passage over MN as evident by 00z sounding from MPX which has veered through a deep layer. Pre-frontal cluster of supercells that are spreading across the eastern portions of ww194 will continue moving east across western WI this evening, along with an attendant threat for hail, wind, and perhaps a few tornadoes. ..Darrow.. 05/10/2022

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Elevated thunderstorms may continue to pose an isolated threat for large hail and strong/gusty winds. Watch issuance is possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An elevated thunderstorm cluster has recently strengthened as it moved from eastern SD into southwestern MN. This convection is occurring on the nose of a 50-60+ kt southerly low-level jet, and a strong mid-level southwesterly jet is also present over this region. Related 50-70+ kt of effective bulk shear are proving very favorable for updraft organization, with clear evidence of a hail core aloft with this activity. Low-level moisture is also rapidly returning northward with the low-level jet, and MUCAPE has increased to around 1000-2000 J/kg downstream of the ongoing activity. However, based on current thunderstorm structure and radar presentation, it is less clear whether large amounts of marginally severe hail are being produced, or very large hail. Regardless, potential for isolated severe hail will likely persist with these elevated thunderstorms as they spread northeastward this morning across parts of central MN. Strong/gusty winds may also occur. Watch issuance is possible, especially if it becomes clear that additional severe thunderstorms will form in the warm advection regime.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe thunderstorms capable of large hail will continue across parts of central Minnesota this morning. This activity may continue to pose a severe threat into parts of northwest Wisconsin over the next 2-3 hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Fast moving, elevated severe thunderstorms continue to pose a threat for large hail this morning. This activity is quickly approaching the eastern edges of greater elevated instability on the nose of a strong low-level jet and warm advection regime. The 12z RAOB from MSP shows very steep 700-500 mb lapse rates and strong vertical shear, supporting continued organized cells capable of large hail. With northeastward extent a gradual weakening trend is expected. However, severe hail will continue to be possible across northeastern portions of WW 192 and may spread into a small portion of northwest WI over the next 2-3 hours before sufficient weaken below severe limits occurs. As a result, a small downstream watch will likely be needed soon. ..Leitman.. 05/09/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe hail will continue to be possible across WW 193 for the next hour or so.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An intense elevated supercell continues to produce severe hail up to 1.75 inches in diameter as of 1640z. While MRMS MESH has weakened, the supercell still appears to be well-organized in KDLH 88-D data. Specifically a three-body scatter spike is noted in addition to very low differential reflectivity signatures, both being indicative of large hail. MUCAPE is steadily increasing with eastward extent, keeping pace with the progression of the supercell, and coincident with a strong 850 mb low-level jet and warm advection regime. This may continue to support severe hail for another 1-2 hours given steep midlevel lapse rates and favorable shear. It is unclear if a downstream watch will be needed for portions of WFO GRB and MQT, but trends will be monitored over the next hour or so as the Sawyer County WI supercell shifts east/northeast. ..Leitman.. 05/09/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The airmass across southern MN into northern IA is rapidly destabilizing and severe potential is increasing. A tornado watch will likely be needed by 20-21z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The airmass across southern MN into far northern IA is rapidly recovering from morning convection and quickly destabilizating. Mid to upper 60s F surface dewpoints are now widespread across northern IA to near the MN state line as temperatures have warmed into the upper 60s to mid 70s. This is resulting in rapidly eroding MLCIN. Towering cumulus have been noted across southwest MN over the past hour or so as a north to south oriented surface boundary/dryline quickly progresses eastward. A warm front is extending southeast from a surface low near Fargo ND toward southeast MN. The warm front is forecast to lift northward into central MN/west-central WI over the next few hours. While large-scale ascent is forecast to remain rather weak, strong vertical shear, both effective and in the 0-1 km layer, steep lapse rates and strong instability will support organized supercells. Weaker forcing will likely limit the number of storms, but one or two intense cells are expected to develop over the next few hours. Current VWP data from the KMPX 88-D near the warm frontal zone already indicated enlarged, favorably curved hodographs with 0-1 km SRH greater than 450 m2/s2. Any cell that develops withing the northward retreating warm frontal zone will have enhanced tornado potential in addition to large hail and damaging gusts.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The tornado and large hail threat will increase into the early evening with any sustained supercell.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Multiple supercells have recently developed across portions of east-central/southeast MN, within a moderately unstable and strongly sheared environment. It remains unclear how many of these cells will mature and become sustained into the early evening, due to the influence of relatively warm and dry midlevels noted in the 20Z MPX sounding. However, strong warm advection downstream is resulting in a narrow corridor of destabilization ahead of these cells, and at least a couple of supercells are expected to spread into northwest WI with time. Very strong effective shear (60+ kt) and 0-1 km SRH of 200-400 m2/s2 (greater with northward extent) will support a conditionally favorable tornado environment for any mature supercell that can be sustained, in addition to a large hail threat. The eastward extent of the greater risk will be determined by how quickly the downstream environment can destabilize as storms move rapidly northeastward. ..Dean.. 05/09/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: If convection can be sustained along the front this evening, a brief tornado and/or strong wind gust will be possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Convection in gradually increasing across northern MN along and ahead of a cold front. Some destabilization is ongoing downstream of this development, though low-level moisture remains relatively limited. Deep-layer shear is quite strong (effective shear of 70+ kt per recent mesoanalyses) across the region, which could aid in the development of an organized storm or two, but may also tend to inhibit deep convection given the limited instability. Any stronger storm that can be sustained will pose a threat of a brief tornado and/or strong wind gusts, given the strong low-level flow/shear resulting from a 50+ kt low-level jet. For now, it appears that the threat will remain too isolated and marginal for watch issuance.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorm development and coverage may increase over the next few hours. A few severe thunderstorms may develop, supporting a large hail risk in addition to a few damaging gusts. A tornado also cannot be ruled out. Conditions are being monitored for the need of a WW issuance.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A towering cumulus field along and immediately ahead of a dryline continues to build across central/north-central IA, where signs of convective initiation attempts have become evident in the Boone County, IA vicinity. A 990 mb surface low and accompanying mid-level impulse continues to track northward while crossing the U.S. border into Manitoba. As such, upper support is lacking across IA, with low-level dryline convergence and late afternoon boundary-layer mixing serving as the primary factors for convective initiation. Upper 60s F surface dewpoints overspread by a well-mixed boundary layer (8 C/km 0-3km lapse rates) are contributing 3000 J/kg MLCAPE. Modest veering in the lowest 3 km supports modestly curved hodographs (evident via RAP forecast soundings and some of the latest KDMX/KDVN VAD profiler data. Any storms that can develop, mature and sustain themselves will likely become supercells. Given surface temperatures exceeding 90F though, supercell structures are expected to be relatively high-based, with large hail and damaging gusts the main threats (given 8 C/km mid-level lapse rates and a well-mixed boundary layer extending past 850 mb in depth). Given the magnitude of buoyancy and modest low-level veering of the vertical wind profile, a tornado cannot be ruled out. Confidence in storm development is not overly high given the overall lack of deep-layer ascent. Still, conditions are being closely monitored for a WW issuance given the presence of the aforementioned favorable thermodynamic/kinematic environment.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for large hail, locally damaging wind, and a tornado or two will continue this evening. Some weakening is expected later tonight, and the need for downstream watch issuance is uncertain.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: At 0045Z, several supercells are ongoing across western WI into far southeast MN. Thus far, less-than-ideal low-level moisture and storm interference have tended to limit the tornado threat, though strong low-level shear/SRH (noted in recent mesoanalyses and the ARX VWP) remains favorable for a tornado or two with any sustained semi-discrete supercell. Storm interference has also tended to limit the hail threat to some extent, though moderate buoyancy and strong deep-layer shear will continue to support large hail potential through the evening. However, an increasingly linear mode has been noted within the last hour as convection increases along the cold front, which may lead to an increase in the damaging wind potential, but a gradual decrease in tornado/hail risk. Some weakening has been noted across northwest WI, where storms have outpaced the stronger low-level moisture return. Further south into west-central WI/far southeast MN, warmer temperatures and somewhat greater low-level moisture should help to sustain convection as it moves eastward, though eventual weakening is expected downstream of this area later tonight as MLCINH continues to increase. Some severe threat may spread east of WW 194 by 02Z. With the threat expected to diminish with eastward extent later tonight, the need for downstream watch issuance and/or local watch extension is uncertain.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat continues across Severe Thunderstorm Watch #195. Large hail is expected to remain the primary threat, though a damaging gust or two remains possible over the next couple of hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Multicellular storm clusters have increased in both coverage and intensity across portions of central into northeast Iowa as the cold front merges with the dryline, resulting in enhanced low-level convergence. Ample buoyancy remains in place, with the 01Z mesoanalysis depicting 2000-3000 J/kg MLCAPE in eastern IA. These high CAPE values are driven by a well heated/mixed boundary layer, with temperatures still over 80F amid upper 60s F dewpoints. Large hail may accompany the more persistent updrafts, as observed over Mitchell County, IA in the past hour. As long as the boundary layer remains warm/mixed, a couple of damaging gusts may also occur with the stronger storm cores before boundary-layer decoupling sets in over the next few hours. ..Squitieri.. 05/10/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A couple of the stronger storms may produce marginally severe hail and perhaps a damaging gust or two. A WW issuance is not currently anticipated given the isolated nature of the severe threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Thunderstorms have been increasing in coverage as a cold front continues to merge with the dryline, increasing low-level lift. The upper trough and associated surface low responsible for convective initiation farther north across the Upper Mississippi Valley continue to track north, away from the Midwest. Low-level convergence along the cold front is the primary mechanism for convective initiation in the absence of upper support. While ample buoyancy is in place to support a isolated large hail/damaging gust threat, the boundary layer has already begun to cool, with the 02Z mesoanalysis depicting increasing convective inhibition across central into southeast Iowa. While the storms across southern Iowa may continue for a few more hours, boundary-layer decoupling should encourage these storms to become more elevated soon, posing mainly a marginally severe hail threat. Given the expected short-term period of surface-based development and isolated nature of the severe threat, a WW issuance is not expected.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Some severe wind and hail threat may persist into the overnight, but a decreasing trend is expected with time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: At 04Z, strong storms are ongoing across parts of IA/WI, with one line segment noted moving toward central WI, and another moving from northeast IA into southwest WI. The environment remains favorable immediately downstream of this convection, with moderate buoyancy and deep-layer shear noted on recent objective mesoanalyses. In the short term, stronger line-embedded cells will continue to pose a threat of isolated hail, while any small bowing segments (as recently noted southeast of La Crosse) will pose a damaging wind threat. A general weakening trend is expected into the overnight hours, as MLCINH increases, and large-scale ascent weakens in the wake of a vigorous midlevel shortwave trough and surface cyclone that are moving quickly away from the region. A marginal and localized severe threat may spread east of the current watches, but new downstream watch issuance is currently not expected.
